newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Southern Australia still has severe dry - bureau.
newsitem.headline: Southern Australia still has severe dry - bureau.

text.p: The dry period from late spring to early autumn in southern Australia had led to rainfall deficiencies in the region, the Bureau of Meteorology said on Friday.
Rain during the first week in May had been insufficient to alleviate the serious to severe deficiencies over southern parts of mainland Australia, it said in its latest drought report.

For the seven-month period ending April 1997, serious to severe deficiencies existed over a large part of the southern Australian coast and adjacent inland, extending from the southeast of Western Australia (WA) to eastern Victoria and the northeast of Tasmania, he said.
Pockets of driest on record areas were evident in the southeast of WA, the southern Eyre Peninsula of South Australia (SA), southern Victoria and the northeast of Tasmania, he said.

Rainfall deficiencies existed in the northeast corner of Tasmania as the heavy rain and flooding which occurred in the north and northwest of the state during the first week of May failed to reach the northeast corner, he said.
A small area of serious deficiencies existed on the Darling Downs in Queensland, he said.
Long-term rainfall deficiencies for a 20-month period ending in April remained in a region west of Alice Springs on the border between Northern Territory and WA, he said.
A small area of serious deficiencies was now evident near coastal areas of the SA and Victorian borders and near Ceduna in SA, he said.
